glossary.def: A map from each term to the documents that contain it. It serves BM25 and learned sparse retrieval.
A learned sparse retrieval model that assigns weights to terms, including expansion terms, with sparsity regularisation so an inverted index can serve it.
A model that embeds query and document separately, so document vectors can be precomputed and searched fast. Used for first-stage dense retrieval.
The share of questions for which at least one gold chunk appears in the top k results. It is the ceiling for answer quality in RAG.
The shortlist passed to a reranker. In Azure AI Search the semantic ranker receives the top 50 results.
Cleaning, expanding or restating a query, often using chat history, so the index can match it. It can also drift from the original meaning.
Generating several variants of a question, retrieving for each and fusing the lists, commonly with RRF.
Asking the model for a higher-level concept or principle before reasoning. In RAG it adds an abstract question beside the specific one.
Splitting a compound question into sub-questions. Independent parts can run in parallel.
Retrieval where each search depends on what earlier searches found, as in IRCoT. It needs hop, budget and sufficiency limits.
A model turns a natural-language question into a semantic query plus a structured metadata filter. The filter must be validated and never replaces authorization.
In Azure agentic retrieval, `searchIndexParameters.queryHints` stores filter hints and boosts that guide the query-planning model on a search index knowledge source. Best effort, preview.
Corrective RAG: a lightweight retrieval evaluator scores document quality and triggers actions such as web fallback and decompose-then-recompose filtering.
A fine-tuned language model that decides when to retrieve and critiques passages and its own output with reflection tokens.
In Azure AI Search agentic retrieval, the object that holds knowledge sources and a retrieval reasoning effort, and answers the retrieve action.
A connection a knowledge base searches, indexed (search index, Blob, OneLake and others) or remote (web, MCP server and others).
The retrieval planning level in agentic retrieval: `minimal`, `low`, `medium` or `auto`. Higher levels add planning, a classifier and retries.
Microsoft's managed knowledge layer: knowledge bases that many agents can share, built on Azure AI Search, with permission-aware retrieval.
A router that sends each query to RAG or long context based on model self-reflection, aiming for long-context accuracy at lower cost.
Declining reliability of language models as input length grows, even on simple tasks.
Put the gold chunk in the prompt. A wrong answer then points to generation, and a right answer points to retrieval, ranking, filters or context assembly.
Testing whether a cited source span supports a claim, using an NLI model or an LLM judge. A citation alone proves provenance, not support.

claims.text: Azure AI Search BM25 defaults are k1 = 1.2 and b = 0.75.
BM25Similarity is the fixed algorithm on Azure AI Search services created after July 2020, and @search.score has no upper bound.
SPLADE uses explicit sparsity regularisation and a log-saturation effect on term weights so an inverted index can serve it.
The Azure vector search pages read on 2026-10-13 do not document SPLADE-style sparse or late-interaction retrieval.
On EntityQuestions, dense retrievers drastically underperformed sparse methods and generalised only to common entities unless the question pattern was seen in training.
Azure documents cosine vector similarity scores from 0.333 to 1.00 and an unbounded BM25 score.
The vector query threshold parameter drops weak matches before fusion, even when fewer than k remain, and is preview in 2026-08-01-preview.
Azure uses RRF whenever two or more queries run in parallel: text plus one vector query is two executions, text plus two vector queries over five vector fields is eleven.
Cormack et al. (SIGIR 2009) fixed k = 60 in a pilot on TREC collections and found the choice near-optimal but not critical.
Azure does not state the exact RRF constant it uses or a request parameter to change it (UNVERIFIED).
vectorQueries[].weight multiplies a query's RRF contribution and defaults to 1.0. maxTextRecallSize defaults to 1,000 and is a preview parameter in 2026-08-01-preview.
A hybrid query returns the top 50 fused results without paging, and with the semantic ranker k plus maxTextRecallSize should sum to at least 50.
Bruch et al. (2022) found a convex combination of normalised scores beat RRF in and out of domain and that RRF is sensitive to its parameters.
The Azure semantic ranker only reranks the top 50 results, cannot find new documents, and reports @search.rerankerScore from 0 to 4.
The semantic ranker summary string is capped at 2,048 tokens (it was 256 before November 2024), search=* disables it and orderBy with semantic returns HTTP 400.
Cohere rerank-v4.0-pro and rerank-v4.0-fast take 32k context, rerank-v3.5 takes 4096 tokens, and results carry index and relevance_score.
A cross-encoder passes query and document together through a transformer, and Sentence Transformers re-ranks a candidate set of about 100 from the first stage.
Late interaction can inflate index size by about an order of magnitude, which ColBERTv2 addresses with residual compression.
Anthropic reports top-20 retrieval failure rates of 5.7%, 3.7% with contextual embeddings and 2.9% with contextual BM25 added, and a 67% reduction with reranking (vendor numbers).
OpenAI file search ranking_options.score_threshold ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.
Azure warns that the semantic reranker score distribution shifts with infrastructure and model updates, so granular cutoffs are not advised.
Azure queryRewrites accepts generative|count-N with N from 1 to 10, needs queryLanguage set to a supported locale (71 listed) and is preview.
HyDE embeds an LLM-written hypothetical document with a contrastive encoder and retrieves real documents, without relevance labels.
Step-back prompting reported gains on PaLM-2L of about 7% on MMLU Physics, 11% on Chemistry, 27% on TimeQA and 7% on MuSiQue.
RAG-Fusion generates multiple queries and fuses them with RRF, and the study notes answers sometimes strayed off topic.
IRCoT improved retrieval by up to 21 points and QA by up to 15 points on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue and IIRC with GPT-3.
Azure query hints (searchIndexParameters.queryHints) are preview, best effort, not applied at minimal effort, and generated filters are combined with baseFilter and filterAddOn using AND.

LazyGraphRAG (blog 2024-11-25) reports indexing cost equal to vector RAG and 0.1% of full GraphRAG, and over 700 times lower query cost than GraphRAG global search for comparable quality (vendor benchmark).
GraphRAG query modes are Global, Local, DRIFT and Basic, and indexing methods are standard and FastGraphRAG.
RAPTOR with GPT-4 improved the best QuALITY result by 20% absolute.

Agentic retrieval effort levels: minimal (no LLM planning, extractiveData), low (default, one planning pass, 5,000 answer tokens), medium (classifier and one retry, 10,000 answer tokens), auto (preview 2026-08-01).
The stable 2026-04-01 API supports only minimal effort with intents input and extractive output. Planning, answer synthesis, messages input, auto and SSE streaming need 2026-08-01-preview.
If the user identity is omitted from a retrieve call, indexed knowledge sources return unfiltered results, and ingestionPermissionOptions must be set at creation.
Azure OpenAI On Your Data retires on 2026-10-14 and Microsoft recommends Foundry Agent Service with Foundry IQ.
CRAG uses a lightweight retrieval evaluator with web-search fallback and is plug-and-play, while Self-RAG needs a fine-tuned model (7B and 13B reported).
Li et al. found long-context models beat RAG on average when resourced enough, RAG is much cheaper, and Self-Route keeps accuracy near long context at lower cost.
NoLiMa at 32K tokens: 11 of 13 models fell below 50% of their short-context baseline, GPT-4o from 99.3% to 69.7%. Chroma Context Rot (2025-07-14) tested 18 LLMs.
Anthropic Citations enabled together with structured outputs returns HTTP 400, and cited_text is not counted toward output tokens.
ALCE found that on ELI5 even the best models lack complete citation support 50% of the time.
OpenAI file search answers carry file_citation annotations and raw hits return only with include: ["file_search_call.results"].
